title: Introduce session Merkle index and lightweight IO coordinator to reduce KV lookup amplification
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Background: The serving runtime currently suffers from KV lookup amplification during large multiparty sessions: repeated per-slot linear scans of on-disk KV manifests increase tail latency and add noise to continuous batching. This is especially visible for multi-turn chat sessions with long contexts where slot pinning causes many small I/O reads and cache churn. Goals: 1) Reduce per-request KV read amplification and tail latency for long-lived sessions. 2) Keep changes lightweight and incremental so Dedicated/Private deployments can backport. 3) Improve observability so follow-up tuning is easy. Non-goals: full KV store redesign, introducing a heavyweight indexer that requires disruptive migrations.
proposal: Add a compact in-memory 'session Merkle index' keyed by session ID + prefix-hash that summarizes active KV keys for the session and their shard locations. Complement the index with a light-weight IO coordinator responsible for batching and coalescing small reads across concurrent slots and enforcing cooperative backoff between prefetch and eviction workers. The index is append-only and rebuilt lazily per session; it avoids a global lock and keeps memory bounded by using a TTL and sampling. The IO coordinator exposes a request coalescing API used by the batcher and prefetcher to turn many small reads into larger aligned reads and to prioritize reads that will unlock hot slots.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 95th percentile token latency for long chat sessions improves by at least 18% under synthetic mixed traffic. 2) KV read amplification (number of distinct LBA reads per session token) decreases by >= 30% in bench runs. 3) No measurable regression on small single-turn requests (P50 < 5% change). 4) New metrics (session_index_size, io_coordinator_coalesce_rate, index_rebuilds) are emitted to the runtime metrics pipeline and surfaced in the Console dashboard. 5) Feature guarded behind runtime flag: session_merkle_v1 and safe default off for Private until validated.
plan: Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): prototype in unit tests and microbench harness; measure read amplification baseline. Phase 2 (impl, 2 weeks): implement in-memory session index and IO coordinator; add guards and feature flag. Phase 3 (integration & perf, 1 week): integrate with batcher/prefetcher, run scale bench and cluster soak. Phase 4 (monitor & rollout, 1 week): enable on canary fleet with traffic shadowing; collect metrics and adjust TTL/coalesce thresholds. Phase 5 (gradual rollout): gated rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on error budgets.
implementation_notes: - Keep index representation compact: use 64-bit prefix-hash keys and 32-bit shard ids. - Avoid global locks: use per-session shards and RCU-style swap on rebuild. - IO coordinator uses a small fixed-size window to aggregate reads; implement deadline-driven flush to avoid latency amplification. - Add careful instrumentation around prefetch eviction interplay to avoid starvation. - Provide lightweight persistence hooks for Private deployments to warm index from persisted session manifests if enabled.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Index rebuild spikes CPU when many sessions first touch; Mitigation: stagger rebuilds and add exponential backoff. Risk: Coalescing increases P99 for some short tail requests if flush thresholds are mis-tuned; Mitigation: test with microbench and ensure max-wait bound. Risk: Memory usage increases under pathological session counts; Mitigation: TTL eviction and sampling to keep index bounded.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for index correctness and collision handling. - Microbench harness to simulate 1k concurrent long-lived sessions with realistic token arrival patterns. - Chaos test where the IO coordinator is stopped/started to validate graceful degradation. - Integration test in staging that mirrors production SLOs for 48h. - Add regression tests for eviction and prefetch interplay.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature disabled by default. 2) Enable on canary fleet with 1% traffic for 24h; validate metrics. 3) Gradually increase to 10% and run 72h soak. 4) If error budget fine, move to 50% and finally 100%. 5) Keep fast rollback path: runtime flag + orchestrator policy to pin to fallback behavior (no index, existing I/O path).
metrics: Emit new metrics: session_index_entries (gauge), session_index_memory_bytes (gauge), index_rebuilds_total (counter), io_coordinator_coalesce_rate (ratio), io_coordinator_aggregated_reads (counter), kv_read_amplification_ratio (gauge). Track SLI: token_p99_latency_by_session_length and kv_read_amplification_ratio. Add dashboards for these and add alert when kv_read_amplification_ratio regresses > 20% over baseline.
notes: This approach was chosen after a spike showed that the majority of redundant small reads came from repeated per-slot manifest scans. The Merkle index trades a small amount of in-memory metadata for a large reduction in random IO. We intentionally keep the format conservative to allow backporting into Dedicated/Private without a heavy migration.
